fields.title: Every corpus validates and its generated output is fresh
fields.evidence: The `corpora` job's log on the pull request, one run per corpus, plus the `tool` job's template steps.

sections.What it checks:
* `eng:std-GATES.BUILD` says the build "**MUST** run from a clean checkout,
  on an agent that is not a person's own machine".
* `std-VERS.CONSUME` says a consuming corpus "**MUST** move
  the `resolved:` lock of its `consumes:` entry in the pull request moving the producer's `content-version`".
sections.How it works:
The `corpora` job runs `kac validate` and then `kac generate --check` in each of `examples/library`, `examples/engineering`, `examples/payments` and `examples/dog-fooding`. Its `validate` passes `--since` with the branch the pull request targets, so it also compares each record with its state there. The `tool` job runs the same pair in `template/`, without `--since`, and again in a corpus `kac new` created from the packed tool.

Each matrix cell is a fresh runner with its own checkout, and each corpus declares a different `types:`. Running all of them proves the framework works for a corpus that adopted a subset. `payments` and `dog-fooding` pack `engineering` and restore it first, because `.imports/` is not committed.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
`validate` checks a corpus against the schema. It reports a broken reference, a missing section, an unreciprocated edge or a field out of range. It reads no standard, so a record that obeys the schema and none of [std-PROSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/prose.md) passes.

`generate --check` reports stale output and prints the command to run locally. It writes nothing back, because the job has `contents: read`.

`validate` asks each consumed source what it publishes now, once per run. It fails an import that was never restored, and reports where a newer version sits outside the declared range. Where the newer version sits inside the range, as a producer's patch move does, it warns and passes. A patch move with no lock move merges into `main` with a warning. It cannot see another pull request, so a lock moved in a later one passes here.

Most of the types the schema declares have no record in any corpus here, and a rule declared on an empty folder has never run against content. `kac validate` passes a corpus whose types are empty.
